V1.name: Non-visual access to digital text and interface content
V1.definition: Use screen readers or equivalent non-visual representations to read, navigate, and act on digital text, controls, documents, and web content.

V2.name: Magnification and text enlargement
V2.definition: Enlarge text, controls, or the screen through zoom, text sizing, or magnification so content is perceivable and usable.

V3.name: Contrast and display-palette customization
V3.definition: Adjust contrast, foreground/background presentation, inversion, or display palette to improve visual readability.

V4.name: Color-vision differentiation support
V4.definition: Use color filters or non-color cues when color differences are difficult or impossible to distinguish.

V5.name: Access to non-text visual information
V5.definition: Obtain equivalent information from images, maps, charts, infographics, scanned documents, labels, and other visual-only or poorly described content.

V6.name: Accessible CAPTCHA and verification
V6.definition: Complete verification without depending on inaccessible visual perception, including use of alternative modalities or delegated assistance.

H1.name: Speech-to-text access through captions or transcripts
H1.definition: Access spoken and relevant non-speech audio information through captions, live captions, or transcripts.

H2.name: Caption readability and language customization
H2.definition: Configure caption language and visual presentation so caption text is readable and appropriate for the media being consumed.

H3.name: Visual and persistent alternatives to auditory notifications
H3.definition: Receive alerts visually rather than by sound alone and keep visual notifications available long enough to notice and read.

H4.name: Single-channel access to stereo audio
H4.definition: Combine stereo channels so information is not missed when a user hears through one channel or one headphone.

H5.name: Verification without relying on hearing
H5.definition: Complete CAPTCHA or verification when the presented challenge depends on auditory perception, using a non-auditory alternative or delegated assistance.

M1.name: Alternative text entry without a physical keyboard
M1.definition: Enter text through an on-screen keyboard or other alternative input when physical keyboard use is difficult.

M2.name: Sequential modifier-key input
M2.definition: Use multi-key commands one key at a time instead of holding multiple keys simultaneously.

M3.name: Keystroke filtering and sensitivity control
M3.definition: Reduce accidental repeated or brief key presses by adjusting keyboard sensitivity/filtering.

M4.name: Alternative pointer control or delegated pointing
M4.definition: Use keyboard, speech/other alternative input, or delegated pointer activation when conventional mouse use is difficult.

M5.name: Reduced press-hold and dragging demand
M5.definition: Avoid or reduce sustained press-hold-drag-release movements that require dexterity or sustained pointer control.

M6.name: Mouse-button and handedness customization
M6.definition: Configure the primary mouse button or equivalent pointer settings to match reach, strength, dexterity, or unilateral motor needs.

M7.name: Reduced pointer precision, repetition, and timing demand
M7.definition: Avoid or delegate interactions requiring repeated precise target acquisition, tightly timed pointer actions, or fine motor control.

C1.name: Focus, readability, and simplification
C1.definition: Reduce distraction, visual/cognitive clutter, or reading load so attention, language processing, and comprehension are easier to sustain.

C2.name: Memory externalization and short-term retention support
C2.definition: Reduce reliance on working memory or short-term retention by using notes, checklists, persistent cues, or delegated assistance.

C3.name: Time and prospective-memory support
C3.definition: Use reminders, calendars, timers, and persistent time-based cues to manage appointments, deadlines, intervals, and future actions.

C4.name: Planning, sequencing, task-state tracking, and completion recognition
C4.definition: Reduce the burden of unfamiliar or multi-step workflows, maintaining context, tracking progress, recovering after distraction, and recognizing successful completion.

C5.name: Decision and choice support
C5.definition: Help compare alternatives, apply constraints, understand consequences, and select an appropriate option.

C6.name: Important-information extraction and prioritization
C6.definition: Identify and preserve the small set of important facts or actions from dense, mixed, or distracting information.

C7.name: Calculation, counting, copying, and cross-source reconciliation support
C7.definition: Reduce reliance on arithmetic/counting, copying, short-term retention, or reconciling information across sources and steps.

C8.name: Error prevention and safety-critical guidance
C8.definition: Make risky actions, scams, health/safety guidance, and error-prone choices easier to understand and act on correctly.
